record.original_question: Let Omega be a bounded convex domain. Give conditions that ensure the graph of a constant-mean-curvature solution over Omega with planar boundary has positive Gauss curvature everywhere, i.e. is convex as a surface.

evidence.quote: Following (4.1) and phi = 0 along partial Omega, it is natural to ask if a solution of the Dirichlet problem is convex in the sense that the Gauss curvature K of the graph is positive everywhere.
Problem 4.3 (4*). Let Omega be a bounded convex domain. Give conditions that assure the convexity of a cmc graph on Omega and with planar boundary

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded convex domain, and let $H$ be a nonzero real constant. Consider a function $u \in C^2(\overline{\Omega})$ that solves the constant mean curvature equation
$$\operatorname{div}\!\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}\right) = 2H \quad \text{in } \Omega,$$
with planar boundary, i.e. $u \equiv 0$ on $\partial\Omega$ (so the boundary curve of the graph lies in the plane $\{z=0\}$). Let $\Sigma = \{(x,y,u(x,y)) : (x,y) \in \overline{\Omega}\} \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ denote the graph of $u$, and let $K$ denote its Gauss curvature.

Determine geometric conditions on $\Omega$ (and possibly on $H$) that ensure $\Sigma$ is a convex surface, in the sense that $K > 0$ everywhere on $\Sigma$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of identifying conditions on a bounded convex planar domain $\Omega$ that guarantee a CMC graph over $\Omega$ with planar boundary is convex appears to remain open in the Euclidean setting. Related convexity results are known in the Lorentz–Minkowski space (e.g., for spacelike CMC surfaces with pseudo-elliptic planar boundary), and counterexamples are known showing that strict convexity of the boundary alone is not sufficient. No comprehensive sufficient condition for the Euclidean CMC Dirichlet problem appears to be established.

status_evidence.title: Convexity of the solutions to the constant mean curvature spacelike surface equation in the Lorentz–Minkowski space
status_evidence.snippet: For CMC spacelike hypersurfaces with planar pseudo-elliptic boundary, the surface has negative Gaussian curvature and is convex; counterexamples exist for strictly convex boundary in general.
status_evidence.claim: Convexity of CMC graphs with planar convex boundary is delicate; counterexamples exist even in Lorentz-Minkowski setting, and full sufficient conditions are not established.

status_evidence.title: CMC Graphs With Planar Boundary in H^2 x R
status_evidence.snippet: Studies CMC graphs with planar boundary; convexity questions for such graphs over convex domains are posed and partially studied.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of convexity for CMC graphs over convex domains with planar boundary is an active topic with only partial results.
